title: Cross-process file locking behavior is not exercised by the active suite

reasoning: The project relies on file locks for app/CLI shared mutable AWS config state, but the active test only proves sequential read-modify-write accumulation in one process. The only timeout/contention test is explicitly disabled, so an implementation that omits or breaks cross-process fcntl locking could still pass this suite.
recommendation: Add an integration-style Swift test that spawns a helper subprocess to hold the lock, then asserts a second process times out; also add a two-process increment test to prove updates serialize without lost writes.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The file documents that same-process locking cannot model the real behavior, and the subprocess-based test that would cover it is disabled.
suggestedRegressionTest: Spawn a small helper executable or Process invocation that opens `<url>.lock` and holds an exclusive fcntl lock while the parent calls `FileLock.exclusive(on:timeout:)`; assert `.lockTimeout`, then run two helper processes that each call `AWSConfigINIDocument.update` to increment the same key and assert the final count is 2.
minimumFixScope: Add cross-process File IO tests and any minimal test helper target/script needed to hold the fcntl lock.
